record.original_question: For a numerical semigroup S, determine the smallest possible number of irreducible numerical semigroups whose intersection equals S, and decide whether there is a universal constant N such that every numerical semigroup is an intersection of at most N irreducible numerical semigroups.

evidence.quote: We still do not know how many numerical semigroups appear in these minimal decompositions, moreover, we wonder if there exists a positive integer N such that every numerical semigroup can be expressed as an intersection of at most N irreducible numerical semigroups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A numerical semigroup is a subset S ⊆ ℕ = {0, 1, 2, …} that contains 0, is closed under addition, and has finite complement in ℕ (the elements of ℕ \ S are called the gaps of S). A numerical semigroup S is irreducible if it cannot be expressed as the intersection of two numerical semigroups that strictly contain it. It is known that every numerical semigroup S can be written as a finite intersection S = S₁ ∩ S₂ ∩ ⋯ ∩ Sₙ with each Sᵢ irreducible; such a decomposition is called minimal if no Sᵢ may be omitted while still equaling S.

(a) For a given numerical semigroup S, determine the smallest possible integer n for which there exist irreducible numerical semigroups S₁, …, Sₙ with S = S₁ ∩ ⋯ ∩ Sₙ.

(b) Decide whether there exists a universal positive integer N (independent of S) such that every numerical semigroup can be expressed as the intersection of at most N irreducible numerical semigroups.
artifact.status_search_result: Part (b) appears to have been resolved in the negative: subsequent work has shown that the minimum number of irreducibles needed in a decomposition can be arbitrarily large, ruling out a universal bound N. Part (a), determining the exact minimum for a given numerical semigroup, remains an active research topic, with related conjectures (e.g., that the set of decomposition lengths is always an interval) only partially proved (e.g., for multiplicity at most 6).

status_evidence.title: Lengths of irreducible decompositions of numerical semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: the minimum decomposition length of a numerical semigroup can be arbitrarily large; the interval conjecture is proved for multiplicity at most 6
status_evidence.claim: No universal N exists since minimum decomposition length is unbounded; structural questions on minimum lengths remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Numerical semigroups mini-course (García-Sánchez)
status_evidence.snippet: Decompositions of numerical semigroups into irreducibles and minimality
status_evidence.claim: The decomposition framework is standard but the precise minimum number per semigroup is still studied.
